suggestions.title: Forrest Gump
suggestions.description: The history of the United States from the 1950s to the '70s unfolds from the perspective of an Alabama man with an IQ of 75, who inadvertently becomes a war hero, ping-pong champion, and shrimp tycoon while never wavering in his devotion to his childhood sweetheart Jenny. Robert Zemeckis's sweeping, warm-hearted epic — with Tom Hanks's Oscar-winning performance and a flawless period soundtrack — is the rare blockbuster that is both a crowd-pleaser and a genuine American meditation on destiny, chance, and the value of a kind heart. 'Life is like a box of chocolates.'

suggestions.title: The Departed
suggestions.description: An undercover cop infiltrates a powerful South Boston Irish mob gang, while a crime kingpin's mole simultaneously works his way up the Massachusetts State Police — both racing to unmask the other before their cover is blown. Martin Scorsese's electrifying Boston crime saga (finally earning him his long-deserved Best Director Oscar) crackles with a powerhouse cast — Leonardo DiCaprio, Matt Damon, and Jack Nicholson at his most unhinged. A tense, violent, endlessly rewatchable cat-and-mouse thriller that stands among the genre's very best.

suggestions.title: Django Unchained
suggestions.description: A freed slave teams up with a charismatic German bounty hunter to rescue his wife from a brutal Mississippi plantation owner. Quentin Tarantino's audacious, stylish 'southern' reimagines the Western with swagger and fury — Christoph Waltz and Jamie Foxx make a superb duo, while the razor-sharp dialogue, Morricone-tinged score, and explosive set pieces make it pure cinematic fireworks. Equal parts gorgeous, brutal, funny, and satisfyingly cathartic, it's Tarantino at the height of his powers.
